text:
maya: Quick follow-up on shard granularity for onprem delta swaps — leaning toward compact-shard (sub-blob) swaps instead of whole-blob. Need ops/arch take and rollback heuristics. TL;DR: reduce bandwidth, but complexity for verifier and partial apply.

dan: Can you enumerate failure modes? e.g., partial apply stuck, operator needs to roll back mid-apply?

maya: Yeah — off the top of my head:
- partial write corrupted -> tombstone + retry
- checksum mismatch mid-apply -> operator decision point (rollback vs continue)
- dependency ordering (shard A depends on B) -> apply reordering hazards
Thinking we add per-shard apply journal and commit marker to record progress.

srini: Per-shard journal seems fine. How are we guaranteeing cross-shard atomicity? We can't do full transactional commit across many GBs easily.

tess: One pattern: staging dir per node, write shards to staging, then update a manifest with per-shard checksums and a top-level merkle root, finally atomically swap current-manifest symlink. Rollback = symlink back to previous manifest. Downsides: staging storage and extra copy/space.

joel: Symlink swap makes activation quick; cleanup (old shards) can be async. For long rollbacks we should expose an "activation_window" operator knob so human can validate before garbage collection.

maya: Draft config proto: 
```yaml
apply:
  strategy: compact-shard
  staging_dir: /var/redwood/stage
  commit_marker: .commit
  activation_window_seconds: 300  # operator has 5m to validate before async gc
  cleanup_policy: async_with_backoff
  fail_mode: fail-closed  # fail-open allowed for non-compliant dev clusters
```

srini: How does verifier work? We need a signed manifest per-version plus a signed merkle root that covers shard checksums so verifier can avoid fetching whole blobs to validate.

maya: Exactly — each release publishes a signed root and per-shard signed manifests. Node-side verifier validates shard checksum and the shard's inclusion to root. If mismatch, node marks shard tombstoned and reports to operator.

deploy-bot: canary-rollout: compact-shard strategy enabled on pool-3, 10% of nodes (release/2026-03-18). :robot_face:

tess: Also need to think KMS/unwrapping timing: we must ensure keys are available before commit_marker is written. Suggest pre-decrypt during staging and require operator permission if KMS unavailable.

dan: +1 on permission gate. Also add a "rollback_policy" config: 
- immediate-revert (fast symlink swap back)
- staged-rollback (mark previous manifest and schedule background swap at low-traffic window)

maya: I'll add both in RFC follow-up and wire up BDD tests for these scenarios:
```
# simulated failure log
[2026-03-18T14:02:10Z] apply: shard-23 checksum mismatch
[2026-03-18T14:02:10Z] verifier: tombstone shard-23, report -> ops
[2026-03-18T14:03:00Z] operator: selected immediate-revert -> swapped manifest -> activation complete
```

joel: One more ops-UX ask: expose a "preview-manifest" command that shows shard-level diffs and estimated staging size. That will reduce surprise.

maya: Good call. I'll add CLI/Console preview + a GC dry-run. I'll draft the RFC follow-up with config examples and test matrix (partial-apply, mid-verify failure, KMS miss). cc @srini @tess for verifier/key notes. :thumbsup:

joel: :shipit:

dan: minor: include a metric for "partial-applies" and an alert when > 0.1% of activations.

maya: noted — will include metrics and paged runbook for >threshold cases.
